items.title: Key every browser authority epoch to the exact franchise
items.premise: The dashboard already exposes franchiseId, but gameFlow hydration and four app-level background tasks key authority to leagueId or startYear. Dashboard has no leagueId, so two franchises with the same start year and controlled team can share an authority identity and permit an old response to commit after an import or franchise switch.
evidence: gameFlow.dashboardAuthorityKey ignores franchiseId and begins with leagueId || startYear
app.js repeats leagueId || startYear in background-task authority keys at four call sites
authority-epoch tests cover team changes but not two same-year franchises

L1.recipe: Prefer franchiseId in the existing dashboard authority key.

L2.recipe: Create one pure franchise authority helper, use it in hydration and every background task, preserve a safe legacy fallback, and prove two same-year/team franchises reject stale commits.

L3.recipe: Attach authority identity to every loader receipt and expose per-scope stale-discard diagnostics.

verification: franchiseId is the first authority component everywhere
same-year/team franchise switches advance the epoch
legacy dashboards retain deterministic fallback identity
all authority keys come from one helper

items.title: Give save-sensitive browser memory one franchise-scoped authority
items.premise: The Opening Contract tutorial uses one global seen key, Return Digest uses one global last-seen key, and trade-block IDs are written to one global key but never hydrated. A second franchise can therefore lose its Opening Contract offer, receive another franchise's record delta, or inherit/lose trade targets.
evidence: tutorialCampaign hasTutorialBeenSeen reads vsfgm_tutorial_seen_v1 with no scope
mountTutorial runs after dashboard hydration but receives no franchise identity
returnDigest reads franchise-architect-last-seen without storing or checking franchise identity
readTradeBlockIds is imported by app.js but never called; saveTradeBlockIds writes vsfgm:trade-block globally
Priority Inbox already demonstrates a working franchise-scoped persistence pattern

L1.recipe: Scope Return Digest and tutorial keys by dashboard.franchiseId.

L2.recipe: Reuse the pure franchise-scope helper for tutorial, Return Digest, and trade-block persistence; skip tutorial from live startScenarioReceipt, hydrate/reset trade targets when scope changes, reject cross-franchise digest deltas, and add migration/corruption tests.

L3.recipe: Move all save-sensitive browser ledgers behind a versioned storage registry with quota and migration receipts.

verification: a new franchise receives its own Opening Contract offer
an already-contracted franchise never repeats it
Return Digest never compares records across franchises
trade targets restore only inside their owning franchise
storage corruption fails open without blocking play

items.title: Turn the living Season chapter into an exact return action
items.premise: Return Digest renders seasonChapter.nextCall, while the chapter already carries targetTab and targetId, but the digest discards both and offers only Inbox or dismiss. The product names the next decision without letting the player continue it.
evidence: seasonChapters returns targetTab and targetId for every chapter
returnDigest stores the full seasonChapter but renderReturnDigest only interpolates label/title/nextCall
renderReturnDigest actions are limited to jump-inbox and dismiss
game-loop review independently ranked this as the highest bounded retention disconnect

L1.recipe: Add a third button that calls a supplied chapter callback.

L2.recipe: Render a chapter-labeled continuation CTA, pass the exact target as a typed action, activate the target tab, focus/scroll the target element with a safe tab fallback, preserve Inbox/dismiss actions, and cover all action paths.

L3.recipe: Add a non-blocking one-action return rail that also resolves active promise targets and accessibility announcements.

verification: the CTA label derives from the live chapter
the exact target tab and element are honored
missing targets fall back safely without lying

items.category: Feedback loop / game design contract / automation
items.title: Publish and test the intended first-session decision contract
items.premise: The implementation has a strong weekly/season/dynasty loop, but context/GAME_LOOP.md and checked-in playtest evidence are absent. Existing first-session tests always choose the first tutorial option or one fixed combination, so they prove completion without proving all nine choice definitions remain executable and consequence-bearing.
evidence: Playwright chooses the first choice on all three steps
startScenarioContract defines three choices in each of three dimensions

L1.recipe: Add a public-safe GAME_LOOP.md with explicit loop horizons and honesty caveats.

L2.recipe: Publish 30-second, five-minute, season, and dynasty contracts with falsifiable local evidence targets; add an exhaustive 27-combination test proving every Opening Contract choice validates, produces its exact receipt, and survives snapshot restore; document that player outcome claims require a real consented cohort.

L3.recipe: Run and check in a sanitized aggregate of 5-8 consented first-session playtests; never synthesize the cohort.

verification: all 27 Opening Contract combinations execute and restore
each choice produces its declared effect
the public contract names measurable evidence without claiming current impact
no fabricated playtest rows are added
